title: DBC: Drift-aware Binary Code for Drift-tolerant Deep Neural Networks
problem: Phase change memory (PCM) cells with multi-level (MLC) operation suffer from conductance drift over time, causing significant accuracy degradation in DNNs stored in PCM.
motivation: PCM is attractive for DNN weight storage due to high scalability and non-volatility, but drift-induced reliability issues limit practical deployment; improving drift tolerance is critical.
method: Drift-aware Binary Code (DBC) is a binary encoding scheme that makes neural networks resistant to phase change memory's conductance drift—the gradual degradation of memory cell performance over time. It maps smaller decimal values to the most stable levels in the memory cells, so when drift occurs, stored values naturally decrease rather than increase. This works because neural networks tolerate weight reductions much better than weight increases, so storing the most important network weights at the most stable levels keeps accuracy consistent over years of use. The approach requires no additional hardware and works seamlessly with existing error correction codes.
key_novelty: Binary encoding for phase change memory that maps values to minimize conductance drift errors by ensuring that memory degradation shifts stored values toward smaller magnitudes rather than larger ones.
contributions: Novel Drift-aware Binary Code (DBC) targeting PCM reliability
Magnitude-aware value-to-level mapping minimizing drift errors
55.18x improvement in drift tolerance vs. conventional binary code; compatible with ECC
primary_theme: Drift-aware binary encoding for PCM-based DNN storage
